note: The main issuers: Israel's cards are issued by three card companies, Isracard, Max and Cal, not by the banks themselves (chosen as the best-known; no ranking was read). Max's fee page returned an empty page and Cal's site answered 'Request Rejected' on 2026-10-30; neither was read. First International Bank's card tariffs answered with an error page on 2026-10-29. Isracard's tariff of card fees for cards charged to an account by debit authorization (in force from 1 April 2026, version 04/2026), read in full again on 2026-10-30: each card's monthly fee is written (the digital card 9.90 shekels; the local, international and gold card 17.90; the business and platinum card 17.90, written for the platinum; the MORE card 10.90; the cashback+ card 17.90; the Fly Card Premium MasterCard 38.90 and Premium Select 27.90). The local, international and gold card's fee falls to 15.30 at 5,000 shekels charged in the month and is waived at 7,500, and the platinum's at 7,500 and 12,000; the full waivers are written as a waiver on that month's spending (the partial discount isn't modelled). Transactions in dollars, euros or another currency carry a 2.9% fee. Every card's charges are debited from the holder's account each month, written as paid in full; Isracard's credit plans aren't modeled. The World Elite Mastercard, priced at 63.90 dollars a month on a shekel account, the direct debit cards (Isracash, Direct) and the business card aren't written. The cash withdrawal abroad fee (3.5%) is charged on a card paid in full and isn't a cash advance's fee in the game's sense; it isn't written. The card was first read on 2026-10-29 as 'Isracard' (the local, international and gold card), now named for its row.
